clue.text: Cool, very dynamic teen takes on computer work around Los Angeles

indicators.note: takes on is read as takes in, so the rearranged teen holds the next piece
dynamic suggests energetic movement, so the letters of teen are set in motion and rearranged
around means the computer-work letters wrap round the city's abbreviation

parts.note: IT, information technology, is computer work

explanation.surface: A cool, energetic teenager tackles some computing jobs in Los Angeles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dynamic' makes ENTE; 'around' and 'takes on' nest the pieces so ILAT sits inside it. 'Cool' looks like praise for the teen but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To cool a room or person is to air it by letting fresh air circulate, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Beer mostly fills half a dozen small bottles

indicators.note: fills means the trimmed drink goes inside the other letters

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals

indicators.note: mostly means most of the word, losing its last letter

parts.note: ale is beer

explanation.surface: Beer nearly fills six little bottles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims the drink, and 'fills' puts it between the numeral and the size letter; 'half a dozen' is a Roman numeral, not a count of bottles.
explanation.definitionFit: Vials are small glass containers for liquids such as medicine, so they are little bottles.

clue.text: Less bold, I never drunk the last bit of Jägermeister

indicators.note: drunk means intoxicated and reeling, so the letters of I never are jumbled
the last bit means the final letter of the drink's name

explanation.surface: A timid drinker insists they never touched the last drop of Jägermeister, a German herbal liqueur.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' rearranges I NEVER into NERVIE; 'the last bit of' adds R.
explanation.definitionFit: Nervier means more nervous, more jumpy, so less confident and courageous.

clue.text: Working with China's too uncontrolled

indicators.note: uncontrolled means running wild, so the letters are rearranged freely

explanation.surface: A collaboration where China, too, is out of control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uncontrolled' rearranges CHINAS TOO.
explanation.definitionFit: In cahoots means colluding or in secret partnership, so working together with someone, an idiom.

clue.text: Some explicit tapes brought back from Greece

indicators.note: brought back means the letters found are then read in the opposite direction
some means only part of the words explicit tapes is taken

explanation.surface: Some explicit tapes are returned from a trip to Greece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' picks CITTA from explicit tapes; 'brought back' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Attic describes Attica, the region round Athens, so it means Greek, especially classical Athenian.

clue.text: A vegan occasionally coming off as someone who's self-obsessed

indicators.note: off means gone wrong, so the pooled letters are shuffled
occasionally means only alternate letters of vegan, the second and fourth, are kept

explanation.surface: A vegan who sometimes comes across as vain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occasionally' keeps the even letters of vegan; 'off' is the anagram signal, so 'coming off as' does not read as one phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: An egomaniac is a person with an excessive preoccupation with their own importance.

clue.text: Papers in Britain uncharacteristically might produce hard-hitting leaders

indicators.note: leaders are the front runners, so the opening letter of each of these five words is taken

explanation.surface: British papers might, unusually, run punchy editorials.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaders' reads like newspaper editorials, fitting 'Papers', but it signals the first letters of the five words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Bumph is informal British slang for paperwork or tedious printed documents, often unwanted forms and leaflets.

clue.text: Airline covers part of journey back for round fare

indicators.note: covers means sits on top of, which in a down entry puts the airline above the rest

parts.note: BA is British Airways

indicators.note: back means the stage of a trip is reversed

parts.note: a leg is one stage of a journey

explanation.surface: An airline serves part of a return flight, offering a round trip fare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses the stage of the trip, and 'covers' puts the airline on top in this down entry; 'round fare' suggests a round-trip ticket but means ring-shaped food.
explanation.definitionFit: A bagel is a ring-shaped bread roll, so it is food that is round.

clue.text: Guy gets support carrying a big creature

indicators.note: carrying means holding, so the two pieces carry the single letter between them

parts.note: a guy is a man
a tee supports a golf ball

explanation.surface: A man gets help lifting a huge animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carrying' means the man and his golf support hold the single letter between them; 'support' is a golfing tee, not help.
explanation.definitionFit: A manatee, or sea cow, is a large slow aquatic mammal, an example of a large animal.

clue.text: Banal journalist in East London?

indicators.note: in reads as attached to, the editor placed in the borough to finish the word

parts.note: Hackney is a borough of East London
ED, for editor, is a journalist

explanation.surface: Is a tired, clichéd writer one working in East London?
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the whimsy: a hack in HACKNEY. 'journalist' wants to be HACK; it is ED.
explanation.definitionFit: Hackneyed means overused and lacking originality, so trite and unoriginal.

clue.text: A reduced cost for rejected fruit

indicators.note: reduced means the synonym for cost loses its final letter

parts.note: a cost is the price of something

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the short word for 'for' is read in reverse

parts.note: for can mean to, as in a present for (to) you

explanation.surface: Something offered at a discount is turned down in favour of fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced' cuts PRICE to PRIC; 'rejected' turns TO into OT.
explanation.definitionFit: An apricot is a small orange stone fruit, so it is an example of fruit.

clue.text: No cigar is manufactured without the use of chemicals

indicators.note: something manufactured is made up from raw parts, so the letters of no cigar are assembled anew

explanation.surface: A cigar that is made without any chemical additives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is manufactured' rearranges NO CIGAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Organic farming and produce avoid artificial fertilisers and pesticides, so the term describes things grown free of synthetic chemicals.

clue.text: Is Soho's first W Hotel outwardly grand?

indicators.note: outwardly means the three letters sit on the outside, around the opening two-letter word
first means only the opening letter of Soho's is used

parts.note: H is Hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
taken as written

explanation.surface: A question whether a W Hotel in London's Soho looks grand from outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' gives S from Soho's; 'outwardly' puts S, W and H around IS. Soho is a district of central London.
explanation.definitionFit: Swish is informal for smart, posh and fashionable, which matches a sense of grand meaning impressive and luxurious.

clue.text: Fraudster's coke that is cut before a function

indicators.note: cut means the abbreviation for that is is chopped off the slang word

parts.note: charlie is slang for cocaine, coke
i.e. (id est) is the abbreviation for that is
tan, the tangent, is a trigonometric function

explanation.surface: A con man whose cocaine has been diluted before a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' removes IE from CHARLIE, leaving CHARL. 'cut' and 'function' suggest drugs and a social event.
explanation.definitionFit: A charlatan is a person falsely claiming skill or knowledge, a quack or impostor, so a synonym for a swindler.

clue.text: Mathematician somewhere Swiss? Yes, in Geneva entertaining two lecturers

parts.note: Bern is the Swiss capital

indicators.note: entertaining means hosting, so the French word holds the pair of letters inside it

parts.note: oui is French for yes, spoken in Geneva
L is an abbreviation for lecturer, so two of them give LL

explanation.surface: A mathematician is placed in Switzerland, saying yes in Geneva while hosting two academics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entertaining' means the French word hosts the lecturers; French is spoken in Geneva, hence its 'yes'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bernoulli family of Basel produced several famous mathematicians, notably Jacob, Johann and Daniel.

clue.text: Crazy, throwable weapon in a Bond film?

indicators.note: crazy means mad and disordered, so the letters of throwable are scrambled

explanation.surface: A wild thing to hurl as a weapon in a James Bond movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crazy' rearranges THROWABLE. In Goldfinger the henchman Oddjob throws his steel-rimmed hat.
explanation.definitionFit: Oddjob's steel-brimmed derby is the famous weapon of the Goldfinger film, a cryptic example rather than a synonym.

clue.text: Cash-strapped guys outside a bookies

indicators.note: outside means the word for guys wraps around the word for penniless

parts.note: lads are guys
broke means having no money

explanation.surface: Penniless men hanging about outside a betting shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' wraps the guys round the penniless word; the surface's 'outside a bookies' reads as a location but is the containment.
explanation.definitionFit: Ladbrokes is a large British betting firm with high-street shops, so it is a bookmaker's.

clue.text: Being faithful? Pah, at first, that is extremely tricky!

indicators.note: at first means only the opening letter of pah is used
extremely means the extremes, the outer two letters of tricky

explanation.surface: Someone scoffs that keeping the faith is very difficult.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at first' takes P from Pah; 'extremely' takes TY from tricky.
explanation.definitionFit: Piety is devoutness, the quality of religious devotion, which is what being faithful to a creed involves.

clue.text: Order craft beer with crisps mostly

indicators.note: craft is read as a verb, to fashion, so the letters are worked into a new shape
mostly means most of crisps, dropping its last letter

explanation.surface: Ordering a craft beer with a bag of crisps, mostly at the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'craft' looks like craft beer, but it rearranges BEER plus CRISP ('mostly' drops the final S).
explanation.definitionFit: A doctor prescribes medicine by directing its use, and to prescribe is also to lay down a rule.

clue.text: Things used at Hogwarts, provided by owls occasionally?

indicators.note: by is read as among here, the word for provided going in between the two letters
occasionally means only every other letter of owls, the second and fourth, is kept

parts.note: and is an old word for if, provided

explanation.surface: Owls deliver post at Hogwarts, so they might sometimes bring wizards their kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occasionally' takes W and S from owls; AND, meaning 'if' as in 'and it please you', goes between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Hogwarts is the school of witchcraft in the Harry Potter books, where pupils cast spells with magic sticks.

clue.text: Major company debts initially getting settled

parts.note: Nestlé is the Swiss food giant

indicators.note: initially means just the first letter of debts

explanation.surface: A big firm's debts are at first being paid off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes D from debts. 'settled' suggests paying debts but means snuggled down.
explanation.definitionFit: Nestled means settled snugly into a comfortable position, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Dropped dead when pierced with tip of spear

indicators.note: pierced with means a letter is driven into the middle of the word for dead

parts.note: deceased means dead

indicators.note: the tip here is the far end, so the last letter of spear is taken

explanation.surface: Someone fell dead when stabbed by a spear point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tip of' takes R, the end of spear, not its first letter; 'pierced with' sets it inside DECEASED. 'Dropped dead' looks like one phrase but splits.
explanation.definitionFit: Decreased means fell or went down in amount, as prices or numbers drop, a direct verb synonym.

clue.text: Move uneasily at the end of restless sleep

indicators.note: at places the clumsy movement beside that letter, the movement following on
the end means the final letter of restless

parts.note: to lumber is to move heavily and awkwardly

explanation.surface: Tossing and turning after a fitful night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the end of' takes S from restless; LUMBER follows it. 'restless sleep' wants to be read as one phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Slumber is a literary word for sleep, used as both noun and verb.

clue.text: Musician seen and heard all over the place

indicators.note: all over the place means scattered, so the letters of the two words are mixed up

explanation.surface: A performer who is everywhere, visible and audible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all over the place' rearranges SEEN and HEARD together.
explanation.definitionFit: Ed Sheeran is an English singer-songwriter, so he is an example of a musician.

clue.text: Bottom part of wardrobe has thin wood

indicators.note: in a down entry the bottom part is the last letter of wardrobe

parts.note: bony means very thin

explanation.surface: The base of a wardrobe is made of flimsy timber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottom part of' takes E, the end of wardrobe.
explanation.definitionFit: Ebony is a hard dark tropical timber, so it is a kind of wood.

clue.text: One who steals from man in jail

indicators.note: from means the letters are taken out of the run man in jail

explanation.surface: A thief who robs a prisoner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' takes the letters out of mAN IN JAil. 'steals' means moves stealthily, not thieves.
explanation.definitionFit: A ninja is a Japanese warrior trained in stealth, one who creeps silently, which is to steal in the old sense.

clue.text: Pack containing large playing cards

indicators.note: containing means the word for the pack holds the abbreviation inside it

parts.note: a Cub Scout pack is made up of cubs
L is the clothing abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A deck that includes oversized playing cards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pack' looks like a pack of cards, but it is a group of Cubs, junior Scouts.
explanation.definitionFit: Clubs is one of the four suits, so it is a set of the playing cards in a deck.

clue.text: Bolt finally impresses BBC athletics commentator

indicators.note: finally means only the last letter of impresses is used

parts.note: Steve Cram, a former middle-distance runner, commentates on athletics for the BBC

explanation.surface: Usain Bolt at last wins over a BBC athletics pundit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bolt' looks like the sprinter Usain Bolt, but it is the verb, to run off. 'finally' takes S from impresses.
explanation.definitionFit: Scram is an informal command to leave fast, so it means to bolt, run away.

clue.text: Hard infantry at the front line secure elevated ground

parts.note: H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

indicators.note: at the front means only the opening letters of infantry and line are used

parts.note: to lock something is to secure it

explanation.surface: Tough foot soldiers on the front line hold a raised position.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at the front' takes I and L from infantry and line; the military surface hides it.
explanation.definitionFit: A hillock is a small hill or mound, a low raised patch of land.

clue.text: Type of beauty parlour seen in North America, except around Illinois

indicators.note: around means the two outer pieces enclose the state abbreviation

parts.note: bar means except, as in all bar one
IL is the postal abbreviation for Illinois

explanation.surface: A kind of salon found across North America, except near Illinois.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' means the continent's letters and the word for except both enclose the state; 'except' looks like a link but is a piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A nail bar is a salon offering manicures and nail treatments, so it is one kind of beauty salon.

clue.text: Right now, daughter comes in for a hot drink

indicators.note: comes in for means one letter replaces another, the daughter stepping in for the a

parts.note: today can mean right now, at present

explanation.surface: A daughter arrives at once to get a warm drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comes in for' swaps the A in TODAY for D.
explanation.definitionFit: A toddy is a drink of spirits with hot water, sugar and spices, often taken for a cold.

clue.text: Special name given to a racehorse — one that gets beaten!

parts.note: Red Rum is the famous racehorse that won the Grand National three times

explanation.surface: A special name is given to a racehorse, one that gets whipped in races.
explanation.walkthrough: The Grand National is Britain's best-known steeplechase. 'beaten' suggests the horse losing or being whipped, but it is drumsticks.
explanation.definitionFit: A snare drum is struck with sticks, so it is literally something that is beaten in a band.
